newsitem.title: USA: U.S. merger boom led by telecoms, utilities in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. merger boom led by telecoms, utilities in Q3.

text.p: The booming market for U.S. mergers and acquisitions plowed ahead in the third quarter, led by transactions in the telecommunications and utilities sectors, and a resumption of activity in commercial banking, according to statistics released on Tuesday.

More than $152 billion worth of domestic transactions were announced in the third quarter, making it the third-best period recorded by Securities Data Co, a Newark, N.J.-based company that tracks merger activity.
So far in 1996, U.S. firms have announced nearly $439 billion of deals compared with a record-breaking $458 billion set in all of 1995, according to the data.

The pace was led by telecommunications, which announced 70 deals valued at nearly $20 billion in the third quarter. Transactions included WorldCom Inc's $13.3 billion offer for MFS Communications Co Inc.

It marked the second consecutive quarter that the boom was led by telecommunications, which has been invigorated by the Telecommunications Act of 1996 that aims to break down barriers to corporate unions.

The quarterly report issued by Securites Data ranked utilities as the third quarter's second-place leader, with 34 deals valued at about $15 billion. The sector's biggest deal of the quarter was Enron Corp's $3.2 billion bid for Portland General Corp.

Mergers in the banking sector, which slowed in the first six months of 1996 from last year's frenetic pace, picked up steam again in the third quarter. The industry generated $12 billion worth of transactions, led by NationsBank Corp's proposed $9.4 billion purcghase of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.
Securities Data said Morgan Stanley was the leading financial advisor for worldwide merger business in the first nine months of the year, completing 128 deals valued at more than $152 billion.
Skadden Arps Slate Meagher & Flom held the top post so far this year among legal advisors for mergers, with 71 deals valued at more than $125 billion.
